one_line_description.value: Salesforce Commerce Cloud provides B2B/D2C and B2C commerce solutions, with the B2C Commerce API (SCAPI) used to build headless commerce experiences.
one_line_description.quote: Salesforce Commerce Cloud offers distinct solutions for B2B/D2C (business-to-business and direct-to-consumer) and B2C (business-to-consumer) commerce.

has_public_api.quote: Use B2C Commerce API (also known as Salesforce Commerce API or SCAPI) to build headless commerce experiences.

api_type.quote: To further leverage existing development tools, B2C Commerce provides a framework enabling developers to write custom script code, such as controllers, and expose this functionality as a custom REST API under the SCAPI framework.

api_breadth.value: REST, broad: ~600 Commerce API operations spanning Shopper and Admin API groups (read-write, incl. cart, orders, products, sites)

docs_url.quote: Develop personalized ecommerce experiences with our fast, flexible solutions.

auth_methods.quote: For resource access, you must use a client ID and client secret from Account Manager to request an access token. The access token is used as a bearer token and added to the Authorization header of your API request.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: You must include `sfcc.sites` (read-only access) or `sfcc.sites.rw` (read-write access) and other relevant scopes in the client ID used to generate the token. For a full list of permissions, see the Authorization Scopes Catalog.

access_model.quote: To access an on-demand sandbox, you must purchase sandbox credits, enable appropriate permissions and users, and configure a client API ID.

access_notes.value: API access requires a provisioned B2C Commerce organization; client ID/secret are issued via Account Manager and exchanged for bearer tokens. On-demand sandboxes require purchased sandbox credits, and some documentation/links are restricted to existing customers. No self-serve free/trial developer tier appears in the evidence; the fetched Salesforce pricing page gives no Commerce Cloud plan details or self-serve purchase path.
access_notes.quote: Only existing customers can access some of the links on this page.

community_mcp_servers.quote: Empower your AI agents to seamlessly navigate headless storefronts, manage e-commerce orders, and interact with complex SCAPI/OCAPI endpoints natively.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: Create and manage your own sandbox environments as you need them.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: URL-path major versioning: API version comes from the OAS info.version field and is reduced to its major segment (e.g. 1.0.1 → v1) for SCAPI/custom API URLs; SCAPI publishes dated release notes and references a separate Change Policy.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: The API version is located in the `info.version` field and is transformed into a URL version by using the major version segment and prepending it with `v` (for example, `1.0.1` → `v1`).

verdict_reason: SCAPI is a large, publicly documented REST API with documented client-credential/bearer auth, scope catalog, hooks extensibility, and on-demand sandboxes, so it is technically buildable. However, credentials only exist inside a provisioned B2C Commerce organization and even test sandboxes require purchased sandbox credits, with some docs restricted to existing customers. No self-serve free or trial developer tier appears in the evidence, and the fetched Salesforce pricing page gives no Commerce Cloud self-serve path, so the access gate keeps this at moderate.
main_blocker: Requires a paid B2C Commerce org; sandbox/API access depends on purchased sandbox credits
outreach_reason: A developer cannot self-serve an org or sandbox: sandbox access requires purchasing sandbox credits on an existing B2C Commerce account, and Salesforce directs pricing/integration questions to a sales representative rather than a public signup.
open_questions: Disambiguation: 'Salesforce Commerce Cloud' spans B2C Commerce (SCAPI/OCAPI) and B2B/D2C Commerce; this record covers the B2C Commerce API (SCAPI) documented at developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce.

Rate limits: no numeric limits were present in the fetched sources; a search snippet mentioned a Circuit Breaker mechanism for Custom APIs (sfra custom-apis guide) but the source text needed to quote it was not in the bundle.
Webhooks: only server-side Hooks extensibility was found; no evidence of outbound webhooks/event callbacks. Confirm whether a webhook/event subscription feature is documented elsewhere.

sdk_languages: GitHub check found SalesforceCommerceCloud/commerce-sdk and commerce-sdk-core (Node.js) and npm lists @salesforce/b2c-tooling-sdk, but none of those pages are in SOURCES, so official SDK languages could not be cited.

official_mcp_server: value points to Salesforce's @salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp developer-tooling MCP server (npm package authored by Salesforce, local npx/stdio distribution) rather than a hosted commerce-API MCP endpoint; confirm whether this counts as an 'official MCP server' and whether a hosted endpoint exists.
api_breadth: the '~600 operations' figure comes from Salesforce's npm package README, not the official API reference index; the exact endpoint/resource count is unverified.

composio_toolkit_exists: catalog search used the exact phrase 'Salesforce Commerce Cloud' and returned 0 items; verify whether a matching toolkit exists under another name (e.g. 'Salesforce Commerce', 'SFCC', 'SCAPI').

Pricing: the fetched pricing page (salesforce.com/pricing) is generic and shows no Commerce Cloud plan amounts or self-serve checkout, so the paid_plan_required classification rests on the sandbox-credit purchase requirement.
